content.title: How Do I Become a Candidate?
content.summary: To become a candidate for the City Council in Arvada, individuals must be U.S. citizens, at least 18 years old, and residents of the city for at least one year prior to the election, with district-specific candidates needing to reside in their respective districts. City Council members represent constituents, make legislative decisions, and are involved in various boards and committees, with meetings typically held on the first four Tuesdays of each month. Candidates must also adhere to state election and campaign finance laws.
content.body:
In addition to reviewing the information below, to better understand the City, City Council and the election process candidates are encouraged to attend City Council meetings and meet with the City Clerk.

## Background Information

1. [Deciding to Run](#tabf1c146f6-ab36-4e96-ba64-2d0623186548_0)

## Qualifications to Run for City Council

- be a United States citizens
- at least eighteen years of age
- qualified elector of the City of Arvada for at least one year prior to the election date
- candidates for a specific district must reside within that district

## Role and Responsibilities

As a City Council member, your job is to represent your constituents and make legislative and policy decisions for the good of the community.

Council is expressly prohibited by Charter from personnel management issues for employees, with the exception of those appointed directly by Council. The City Manager is the liaison between City Council and staff activity.

### Job descriptions

- [Mayor](/DocumentCenter/View/1995/Job-Description-Mayor)
- [Mayor Pro Tem](/DocumentCenter/View/1994/Job-Description-Mayor-Pro-Tem)
- [Councilmember](/DocumentCenter/View/1993/Job-Description-Council-Member)

## Time Commitments

### Meetings and work sessions

City Council meetings are generally held on the first four Tuesdays of each month. The first and third Tuesdays are typically business meetings and the second and fourth Tuesdays are typically workshops. (5 pm to 8 pm)

### Council retreats

City Council holds two or three retreats each year to discuss long-range goals and budget needs. These are usually held during the day, may be two-day events, and could include a Saturday.

### Other Time Commitments

City Council members are appointed to various boards, commissions, and committees that meet outside of City Council. Time commitments vary greatly with the specific needs of each group.

The time you spend visiting with your constituents will vary, but you need to be willing to dedicate whatever time this takes. There are no “days off” from being an elected official.

1. [The City and City Council](#tabf1c146f6-ab36-4e96-ba64-2d0623186548_1)

## About City Government

Arvada is a home rule city. This means that we have adopted our own city charter, rather than deferring to Colorado statutory law.

The city charter established the city’s form of government as Council-Manager. This means the City Council is the legislative body that determines laws and policy for Arvada. The City Manager, along with staff, is charged with carrying out the decisions of City Council and for the administration and day-to-day decisions required in the operations of the City.

## About City Council

There are a total of six Council members and one Mayor. Each of Arvada’s four districts has one Council representative, and two Council members represent the city at-large. The Mayor is also elected at-large. Four-year terms are staggered. Arvada opted out of term limits by voter approval at the November 1994 election. Council members and the Mayor may serve three consecutive terms in the same office.

## Resources

The following resources give background information about Arvada’s government and the work the City Council and the City have underway.

- [City Charter](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTICH)
- [City Code](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=19934)
- [Strategic Plan](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=5b9502f9b06a9)

1. [Election and Campaign Laws](#tabf1c146f6-ab36-4e96-ba64-2d0623186548_2)

## State election and campaign finance laws

All candidates for municipal office must comply with the requirements of the Fair Campaign Practices Act and Article XXVIII of the Colorado Constitution.

The following resources outline and explain state law regarding elections and campaign finance. It is essential that you and/or your campaign treasurer fully understand what is required of you as a candidate, candidate committee or issue committee.

These resources are intended as a summary of key points for municipal candidates, and does not replace qualified legal advice.

- [Colorado Constitution, Article XXVIII, Campaign and Political Finance](https://advance.lexis.com/documentpage/?pdmfid=1000516&crid=82cb63d1-cd93-4eb3-9b3b-796b72e4e915&action=pawlinkdoc&pdcomponentid=&pddocfullpath=%252Fshared%252Fdocument%252Fstatutes-legislation%252Furn%253AcontentItem%253A61VF-9YF1-DYDC-J092-00008-00&pdtocnodeidentifier=AABABDAAB&config=0143JAAwODgxYWIyNi1mNGJlLTQwYmItYmE4Ni0yOWY2NzQzMjE3MTAKAFBvZENhdGFsb2ecqetP0coiYGhC4QCG46NJ&ecomp=h2vckkk&prid=5a2546a2-c213-4752-87d3-c4d3bb4ab39f)
- [Colorado Revised Statutes, Title I Article 45 (PDF)](https://leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/images/olls/crs2024-title-01.pdf) (Fair Campaign Practices Act can be found on page 509)
- [Election Rules (8 CCR 1505-1)](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/rule_making/CurrentRules/8CCR1505-1Elections.html)
- [Colorado Campaign and Political Finance Manual (PDF)](https://www.sos.state.co.us/pubs/elections/CampaignFinance/files/CPFManual.pdf)

## City election resources

The following resources point directly to the sections of the city charter and city code which address elections, and other documents directly relevant to the election.

- [City Charter, Chapter 3, Elections](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTICH_CHIIIEL)
- [City Code, Chapter 30, Elections](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH30EL)
- [City of Arvada City Council District Boundary Map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/PublicInformation/index.html?appid=5768f3a62e1c4b389ca611a58e3cfef1)

## Paperwork: Timeline and Instructions

1. [Becoming a Candidate](#tab53dd5e52-7813-4c8b-8b90-ad9bd0ed6f27_0)

According to the State of Colorado’s Fair Campaign Practices Act (FCPA) and Article XXVIII of Colorado’s Constitution you become a candidate if you have publicly announced an intention to seek election and have received a contribution or made an expenditure in support of your candidacy.

Prior to receiving a contribution or making an expenditure you must:

- Set up a bank account in accordance with the provisions of [Colorado Constitution Article 28, Section 3(9)](https://advance.lexis.com/container?config=0155JAAyMzg2MTYzZi1jMWNlLTRlOTQtODVjZS0xZTU0MDg1YmQ0OTUKAFBvZENhdGFsb2eEcVf2aFZwpM1qua3EYcVa).
- File a [Committee Registration Form](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=5b97d14d40bd0) with the City Clerk

Within 10 days of becoming a candidate you must:

- File a [Candidate Affidavit Form](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=5b97d14d3c1da) with the City Clerk

You may also choose to:

- File a [Voluntary Code of Fair Campaign Practices Form](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=5b97d14d470ba) with the City Clerk

**Candidates often file all three forms at the same time. You may do so by email, mail, or in person.**

1. [Getting on the Ballot](#tab53dd5e52-7813-4c8b-8b90-ad9bd0ed6f27_1)

To be nominated for the election ballot, you must complete a [Candidate Nomination Petition](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=7efdd8c1348f9) by obtaining the signature of 25 electors registered within the geographic area you are running to represent.

## Rules for Signatures

- Candidates for mayor or an at-large seat need 25 signatures from any elector who resides in the city
- Candidates for a district seat need 25 signatures from electors who reside in the district they seek to represent
- A person may not sign more than one petition for the same seat
- A qualified elector may sign one petition for their specific district, one for an at-large position and one for Mayor

## Circulating the petitions

- Candidates may choose to circulate their own petitions or have other people circulate petitions for them.
- The circulator of the petition must
  - sign the Affidavit of Circulator section
  - have that signature notarized
- The candidate must
  - fill out the Acceptance of Nomination section
  - have that signature notarized
  - fill out their name exactly as they would like it to appear on the ballot

## Timeline for Petitions

- Aug 5 – Circulating of nomination petitions may begin
- Aug 25 – Candidates must file petitions with the City Clerk’s office by 5 pm

The City Clerk’s Office will check the signatures on each petition. You will be notified if you do not have enough valid signatures and given the chance to amend your petition form.

**Nomination Petitions must be delivered as a hard copy (paper) in person, and must be received by 5 pm on the due date.**

1. [Filing campaign finance reports](#tab53dd5e52-7813-4c8b-8b90-ad9bd0ed6f27_2)

Candidates are required to report contributions and expenditures in four different reports throughout the election season.

The Fair Campaign Practices Act requires that you file each [Report of Contributions and Expenditures (FCPA form)](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=5df03ace06ec7) with the City Clerk’s Office. These must be filed by 5 pm on the due date.

The penalty for late filing is $50 per day. Failure to file any reports required under these provisions may be considered a class two misdemeanor.

| Filing | Due Date | Reporting period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1st | Sep 22 | Everything through Sep 15 |
| 2nd | Oct 14 | Sep 16 to Oct 9 |
| 3rd | Oct 31 | Oct 10 to Oct 26 |
| 4th | Dec 4 | Oct 27 to Nov 29 |
FCPA filing due dates and reporting periods

**You may file these reports by email, mail, or in person.**

## How to File Paperwork with the City Clerk

1. [Email](#tabfbd86464-b471-472a-87ce-b354003301e3_0)
2. [In Person](#tabfbd86464-b471-472a-87ce-b354003301e3_1)
3. [Mail](#tabfbd86464-b471-472a-87ce-b354003301e3_2)

1. [Email](#tabfbd86464-b471-472a-87ce-b354003301e3_0)

Email your documents to City Clerk, [Kristen Rush](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#214a53545249614053574045400f4e5346).

Documents are due by 5 pm on their due date.

Please include the name of the document you are filing in the subject line.

1. [In Person](#tabfbd86464-b471-472a-87ce-b354003301e3_1)

Deliver documents in person to the City Clerk's Office at City Hall during regular business hours.

City Clerk's Office (Third Floor)  
8101 Ralston Road  
Arvada, CO 80002

Monday to Friday  
8:30 am to 5 pm

1. [Mail](#tabfbd86464-b471-472a-87ce-b354003301e3_2)

Mail your documents to:

Kristen Rush  
City Clerk's Office  
8101 Ralston Road  
Arvada, CO 80002

Documents are due by 5 pm on their due date.

Please note: postmarked dates are not relevant in determining whether a deadline was met. Documents will only be considered on time if the City Clerk has **received** them before 5 pm on the due date.

Delivery by email (when allowed) and in person are preferred over mail.
